summary: Repaired two independent causes of false/failed served V11 verification without creating a parallel publisher: (1) hardened both existing served Chromium workflows so they require public byte identity for every asset mutated by this job (v11.js and data-layer.js) before browser execution, and (2) found and fixed the reload-only cached hydration crash in data-layer.js (const cached reassignment -> let cached) with a verified one-line net diff. The route retry fix is already served. Publishing the clean data-layer blob to gh-pages could not complete without force because the branch was moving every few seconds under concurrent live/worker publication; multiple bounded no-force CAS attempts lost clean fast-forward races. Force was not used. The new CI is correctly held at the mutated-cut identity gate until that served asset converges, so it can no longer certify stale/partial V11 bytes.

tests.detail: The served v11.js route-retry blob converged and passed byte identity before Chromium in run 36942104210.
Fresh browser evidence isolated reload timeout; source inspection identified const cached reassignment in the cached load path, which throws before semantic hydration.

Net compare from pre-change parent to e4ba14ba shows exactly one functional line changed in data-layer.js: const cached -> let cached. An accidental emergency reference mutation was detected by diff and repaired before Pages publication.
Both existing served CI workflows now block Chromium until v11.js and data-layer.js public bytes match their checked-out source blobs in the same gate iteration.

main clean blob is 5911143ae13ec66c7a9feee813ec68a908418487 while gh-pages remained on the older cached-load blob during bounded attempts; workflow run 36943134870 is held at the mutated-cut identity gate.
Repeated no-force gh-pages fast-forward/content writes lost races to concurrent live and worker-lab publishers (422 non-fast-forward / 409 branch movement). Force was intentionally not used.
No CURRENT/PROMOTED/HUMAN_ACCEPTED mutation, no force update, and no parallel publisher was created.
